$comment: Written by tools/corpus-read-census.mjs. A corpus of 10^5 turns in a real SQLite file, then three timings: the read (`corpus.sessions()`), the assembly (`answerSessions` over the same array with a stub reader at the registered 48k room), and the two together through `askStored()`. Each is the fastest of 3 runs, because load only adds time and the gate compares two of them. The ratio is the registered falsifiable clause: above 2.0 the read-amplification design does not hold and `askStored` is withdrawn in favour of `remember` alone.
dataset: 100000 turns, 500 sessions x 200, one SQLite file
reading: read / assemble. One number, because the clause is one comparison: does the transcript scan cost more than twice the work the answer path was already doing over the same turns?
